title: SATA FIS (Frame Information Structure)
summary: A SATA FIS is the unit of communication between host and device. Types: Register H2D (0x27), Register D2H (0x34), DMA Activate (0x39), DMA Setup (0x41), Data (0x46), BIST (0x58), PIO Setup (0x5F), Set Device Bits (0xA1). The most common is Register H2D (host to device): 20 bytes containing command, features, LBA, device, count, etc.

structure.meaning: 0x27 Register H2D, 0x34 Register D2H, 0x39 DMA Activate, 0x41 DMA Setup, 0x46 Data, 0x58 BIST, 0x5F PIO Setup, 0xA1 Set Device Bits.
ATA command (0x25 READ DMA EXT, 0x35 WRITE DMA EXT, 0xEC IDENTIFY DEVICE, 0xEF SET FEATURES, 0xF8 READ NATIVE MAX ADDRESS EXT, ...).
LBA bytes 0-2 (for 28-bit) or bytes 0-2 of 48-bit LBA.

ext.example_decoded: SATA Register H2D FIS: command 0x25 (READ DMA EXT), LBA 0, count 1
notes: SATA FISes are transmitted over the SATA link (differential signaling).
AHCI (Advanced Host Controller Interface) is the standard SATA host controller.
NCQ (Native Command Queuing) allows up to 32 outstanding commands.
